label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: The designer wrote a third note. Dev built the designer's first.
findings.why: A run of short sentences naming six agents and their hand-offs reads as a list, and I cannot tell who is who yet.

findings.quote: Each member woke at its own minute, did one step of its queue with its reviews, and closed.
findings.why: 'Wake', 'queue', 'reviews' and 'its minute' are used as known terms; as a team member skimming on a phone I need one plain line on what a wake is.

findings.quote: A request not picked up at one session is picked up at the next. Nobody chasing it.
findings.why: The same 'asked at one session, answered at the next, nobody chased it' point is made again at lines 123 and 180.

findings.quote: Three rounds, one picture, and I started none of them.
findings.why: The three rounds are told in the paragraph, drawn in the figure and summed up again at line 180.

findings.quote: Hours of work nobody started, and what it had produced was a queue only I could clear.
findings.why: The queue at one door is said here, in the hour-fourteen scene, and again in the closing summary at line 180.

findings.quote: Every wake started by the clock. Every wake with its five stages.
findings.why: The closing paragraph is a run of fragments that recaps the whole chapter in a list, which a hurried reader will skip.

findings.quote: looked in its mailroom, and found nothing
findings.why: The mailroom is not explained here, and for my own team it is the thing I most want to understand (how requests reach an agent).

findings.quote: The team is temporary. The record is not.
findings.why: Two short declaratives in the manner of a slogan; the thought could run as one sentence.

findings.quote: This is this book's conductor, not the talk's, and this book's storyteller and researcher too
findings.why: I stall on whose conductor is whose, with three teams in play; and it then says I meet the team 'properly in the next chapter', which sends me away mid-scene.

findings.quote: Then a line about the old session, which I leave out here.
findings.why: The omitted line is announced at line 63 and again here.

findings.quote: It tells the new session who it was, where its files are, what it was in the middle of
findings.why: This summary of the handover's contents is then walked through section by section from line 65, so the content is told twice.

findings.quote: Writing the handover you would want today is a good test of yours.
findings.why: It is an instruction to the reader that also grades their own handover; an invitation would sit better.
Twelve self-introductions open the same way, and a table of the same members follows, so the cast is told in three forms.

findings.quote: You do not need all of these to start.
findings.why: It tells me what I need, and is the sentence my team most wants answered (how many agents to begin with), but it gives no answer in the printed text.

findings.quote: The order of the times was right. The order of the work was not.
findings.why: The historian's paragraph on dev's page of rules and parent commits is dense with repository detail I cannot follow without knowing what a merge or parent is; the lesson at line 118 repeats it.

what_holds: 09-nine-hours-with-nobody-starting-work.md: the partial wake that says it is partial (lines 26-30) is exactly the habit I would want from my own agent, and it is concrete.
09-nine-hours-with-nobody-starting-work.md: the empty queue and the maker with nothing to make (lines 164-168) is a clear picture of a bottleneck on the person.
20-sessions-end.md: a session is not a member, and the role lives in files not in the run (lines 24-30), answers my question about agents that forget.
20-sessions-end.md: the walk through a real handover's headings (lines 65-73) is something I could copy on Monday.
21-the-second-factory.md: the failures kept, especially the usage limit evening (lines 96-102), are honest and show a rule failing and being reported.
notes: As a conference team member the question I carry is whether each of us could run with our own agent before the event; the three sections give me the handover shape and the failure habits, but chapter 9 asks me to follow nine hours of agents I have not yet met, and I would skim it on a phone.
